title: Management Thought Explained Simply | Principles of Management Ep 7
description:
How did management ideas change over the last hundred years? In this animated lesson, Ravi's chai stall now has six people on the team, and we walk the road of management thought one stop at a time to find the best way to run it.

You will learn the classical approach (Taylor's scientific management in 1911, Fayol's principles in 1916 and Weber's bureaucracy), the neo-classical or human relations approach (the Hawthorne studies from 1924 to 1932 and Elton Mayo), and the modern approaches (the systems approach of the 1950s and 1960s and the contingency approach of the 1960s and 1970s).

This is Episode 7 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.

In this video:
0:00 Six people, one big question
0:16 Every idea grew from the one before
0:21 What is the evolution of management thought?
0:35 Stop 1: the classical approach
1:09 Stop 2: human relations and the Hawthorne studies
1:39 Stop 3: systems and contingency
2:11 The whole road
2:15 Quick check
2:26 Recap

Next episode: Scientific Management - F.W. Taylor.
